GetLandscapeById.ProjectStatusSummary: CW51 - 2025:1) Overall StatusOverall delivery: On track, with several operational and security-related workstreams progressing in parallel.Key dependency: Final alignment on commercial/invoicing mechanics for the technical conversion (SUM) activity classified as an Additional Service.2) Key Milestones AchievedDR test completed and follow-up actions are being consolidated.Progress continues across security hardening, profile parameter alignment, performance tuning, patching, and conversion preparation.3) Current Priorities and Top Topics- Commercial / Invoicing Topic: Additional Service (Technical Conversion via SUM)The technical conversion execution using SUM (performed by ECS) is an Additional Service.Allianz is asking how this should be invoiced and under which PO it can be booked. This is an internal Allianz topic but we are trying to support as much as we can.Internal Allianz constraint: A new PO typically requires an associated budget, and a new PO may require a new contract, depending on internal governance.Allianz additionally asked whether unused CAS packages from the RISE contract could be leveraged instead of creating a separate PO / contract for this Additional Service.SAP’s current position (as understood from Roman’s feedback):Standard approach for the conversion services contract: signature + PO of the same amount.No direct linkage between CAS packages and these Additional Services is currently recognized.Decision needed: Confirm the viable commercial/invoicing route for SUM conversion (e.g., separate PO under services contract vs. alternative mechanism), and provide Allianz a clear recommendation.CW47 - 2025: - DR test (15th of Nov) was successful without any blockers. Both teams, Allianz and SAP prepared the DR test by organizing sync meetings and aligning. On the DR test day TSM, CDM and EDS EOS team worked together and provided the customer with a successful DR test.- Technical Conversion update: the customer asked for guidance regarding the approach, cost and timeline of the conversion. Once all his questions answered they confirmed that the Conversion will happen 2026 all while working on simplification items now.- CAS packages topic that might have an impact on ALL Allianz contracts: We were unable to start the delivery of the CAS Application Monitoring Service for the IMA team because they have not provided access to their systems/business clients. Without this access to their application layer, the CAS team cannot begin delivery or provide value.The IMA team has indicated that, due to internal challenges, they are currently unable to grant this access.At present, we are delivering the CAS Application Security Updates Service, as it only requires 000 access and does not depend on business client access.To move forward, we see two possible options:If the IMA team can provide business client access, we can start delivering the CAS Application Monitoring Service as planned.If not, we can consider converting/swapping the CAS Application Monitoring package to CAS Application Security Updates. This service can also be extended to other teams within Allianz beyond the IMA team.CW40-2025: - SBX Contract Correction: During S2D handover it was identified that a SBX already existed since July. A misstep correction was coordinated by CAA, PL, and CDM. The new SBX contract was transformed into an uplift for the FMX system while still provisioning the SBX environment.- Delivery Assurance: SBX post-processing prioritized to meet Oct 25th delivery date. Achieved on time. Customer today (29.09) opened an SR for system refresh.- Technical Conversion: Customer evaluating cost approval. CDM clarified Additional Services billing process. Feedback expected next week.- Evidence Request: Customer informed transparently that evidence is billable (to avoid Simplify precedent). Decision expected on 30.09.2025.- Security Audit Contact: Customer requested a dedicated person. Audit team confirmed support but cannot allocate a single dedicated FTE.CW37-2025: A successful migration happened with a Go-Live on the 19th of May.Currently the client is preparing for a Conversion. The details and workshops have been held. On the Functional Conversion side the customer is still in talk on preparations and setting some project dates. On the technical migration side, waiting on the approval from the customers side.
GetLandscapeById.ScenarioSolution: SAP S/4HANA Cloud, private edition, SAP ERP, SAP Webdispatcher, Unmanaged IaaS WTS service for customer, Adobe Document Server
GetLandscapeById.BusinessImpact: The SAP landscape delivered under the Allianz IMA PTO contract supports core business processes including finance, controlling, procurement, HR, and internal operational workflows. Any unplanned downtime of these systems results in immediate and measurable impact across Allianz Technology SE and the broader Allianz Group.Unavailability of the Production ERP or S/4HANA systems would halt critical daily business operations such as journal postings, vendor and customer payments, purchase order creation, invoice processing, and approval workflows as well as the mortgage department. If such an outage occurs near or during the monthly, quarterly, or annual close cycles, it directly jeopardizes the Group’s IFRS and Solvency II reporting timelines and introduces compliance and audit risks. In addition, dependent platforms would also be affected, causing broader operational delays.A Web Dispatcher outage has the same critical business impact, as users would be unable to access the SAP systems entirely, even if backend systems remain operational.Outages in QAS and DEV do not stop business operations, but they significantly disrupt project delivery, release cycles, regression testing, and the ability to transport changes into production. This can delay mandatory regulatory updates, business enhancements, or incident fixes.Finally, during a disaster recovery scenario, failure of the DR landscape to function as contracted would represent a severe continuity risk. Without a viable failover platform, Allianz would be unable to restore operations within the defined RTO/RPO windows, resulting in prolonged service interruption and potential financial and reputational damage.Overall, SAP downtime within the Allianz IMA environment poses high business criticality, with direct consequences on financial operations, internal governance timelines, and the continuity of essential Allianz processes. Daily through the IMA system at Allianz flow 6 billion euros.
